comments.body: At this current iteration I wonder why the logic of persisting the token should be managed in the intergration layer. I believe the API layer would be the better place to handle all the logic of fetching and properly storing the token. Have you tried that? :)

comments.author: author
comments.body:
Thanks for the review. One constraint I should flag: I don't maintain cookidoo-api directly, so each round of changes here requires @miaucl to review a PR upstream and cut a release. We've been through three of those cycles on this change, and I'd rather not keep adding to their queue.

Would you be open to merging this as-is and handling any remaining items in follow-up PRs? If there's anything you consider blocking, I'm happy to address it — it would help a lot if you could list everything in one pass so we can wrap it in a single upstream round-trip.

comments.author: author
comments.body:
Done upstream — `cookidoo-api` 0.18.4 ships miaucl/cookidoo-api#267, and fe62d7f adopts it here.

`Cookidoo` now takes an `on_auth_data_update` callback and calls it from `_apply_tokens()`, so the consumer is notified whenever the tokens actually change: on a login, and on the refresh a request performs on its own once the access token has expired (which is also where the server rotates the refresh token). The library is the only place that knows when that happens, so that is where the signal belongs — it just can't own the *storage*, since where the tokens live is a Home Assistant concern (the config entry).

What that removes from the integration layer: the `persist_auth_data` decorator and the `_AuthDataHolder` protocol it needed, `CookidooDataUpdateCoordinator.save_auth_data()`, the shim on the base entity, and the `auth_data` snapshot at the end of the config flow validation. No call site knows about tokens any more — the client is built with one callback that writes `CONF_TOKEN` back on the entry, and from the config flow one that keeps the pair the entry is created with. Net −60 lines in the integration.

The PR title and description are updated to 0.18.4.

subsequent_commits.message:
Let the library hand us the tokens instead of collecting them

Persisting the tokens was spread across the integration: a `persist_auth_data`
decorator on every call site that could rotate them, a `save_auth_data()` on
the coordinator and a shim on the base entity, plus a snapshot of `auth_data`
at the end of the config flow validation. All of it existed because the
library gave no signal when the tokens changed, so each caller had to look.

cookidoo-api 0.18.4 takes an `on_auth_data_update` callback and calls it
whenever the tokens change -- on a login, and on the refresh a request
performs on its own once the access token has expired. Pass it when building
the client: from a config entry it writes `CONF_TOKEN` back on the entry,
from the config flow it keeps the pair the entry is created with.

No call site has to know about tokens any more, so the decorator, the
protocol it needed, the coordinator method and the entity shim are all gone.

Treat a login parse failure as a connection error in the config flow

The coordinator's _async_setup already maps CookidooParseException to the
retryable setup_request_exception, because login() scrapes the CIAM login
page and can fail to parse it -- a Cloudflare interstitial in place of the
form is the practical case. validate_input() runs the same login() but only
caught CookidooRequestException, so that failure fell through to the generic
"unknown" handler: the user saw "Unexpected error" instead of "Failed to
connect", and a routine upstream hiccup was logged with a full traceback.

Catch it alongside CookidooRequestException, and cover it in the error
parametrization of every flow that validates credentials: both user steps,
both reconfigure steps and reauth.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Catch the parse failure by name in the coordinator

The two handlers that turn a failed login into UpdateFailed caught the base
CookidooException. What they mean is the parse failure that login() can hit
while scraping the CIAM page; the base class also covers
CookidooConfigException, a permanent client defect that would then be
reported to the user as a connection problem and retried forever instead of
being logged as the bug it is. Name the exception that is actually expected,
so anything else keeps its traceback.

The handler for the recovery login lists CookidooRequestException alongside
it: that login() runs inside an except block, so the sibling
"except CookidooException" of the same try cannot catch what it raises.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Create the entry even when the login hands us no tokens

The config flow only ever learns the tokens from the on_auth_data_update
callback, and the library skips it when auth_data is None. That is not a
failure mode: auth_data is None while the refresh token is unset, and
_apply_tokens keeps the old one when a token response omits it
("A refresh response may omit a new refresh token"), so a response without
one is a successful login that notifies nothing. `token` had no default, so
async_create_entry then raised AttributeError instead of creating the entry.

Default it to an empty dict, which is also what the code this replaced fell
back to. cookidoo_from_config_entry() skips a falsy token, so the entry is
set up with a plain credential login and stores whatever that yields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Fall back to a login when the stored tokens cannot be restored

CookidooAuthData(**token) is handed whatever shape the library wrote the last
time the entry was set up, and async_setup_entry awaits it outside any try. A
field the current library no longer accepts therefore raised TypeError and put
the entry in SETUP_ERROR: permanent, no retry, and no way out other than
deleting it -- the one path where a bad stored token did not degrade into a
credential login like every other one does.

Catch it and leave the client without auth data, which is the state the
coordinator already handles by logging in with the credentials.

Also merge the two tests covering the tokens a request rotates mid-update.
They were written when a decorator persisted them in a finally, so the "a
later call fails" case exercised a distinct path; now that the callback writes
them as they arrive, the two differ only in whether a later call raises, which
is a parameter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Name the exceptions the migration expects

The migration caught the base CookidooException, which also covers
CookidooConfigException -- a permanent client defect that would be reported as
"Could not migrate config entry" and lose its traceback. The coordinator was
narrowed for that reason; the migration calls the same login() and
get_user_info(), so list the same three exceptions it does.

Also drop the dead None branch in the test fixture that emulates the library
notifying its consumer: every call site passes a callback now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Persist only the tokens of the validation attempt that succeeded

_save_token runs from the library's callback, which a login that yields no
auth data never fires, so `token` kept whatever an earlier attempt had left
there. An attempt can leave one behind while still reporting an error: login()
notifies as soon as it holds the tokens, and the get_user_info() right after it
can still fail. Retry with different credentials, and a login that hands back
no tokens of its own would persist the pair belonging to the credentials that
were just rejected -- in a reauth, another account's.

Clear it before each attempt builds its client, so what reaches the entry is
only ever what that attempt produced, and an attempt that produced nothing
stores nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Fold the token cases into the user flow test, shorten the docstrings

test_flow_user_success and the two tests that followed it ran the same three
step flow and differed only in what the validation left in the token: the pair
the login handed over, the pair a later request rotated them into, or nothing
at all. That is a parameter, so they are one parametrized test now, with a
helper per case arranging the client.

Also reduce the two callbacks that store the tokens to one line docstrings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

Move the validation token arrangement into a fixture, drop the stored token guard

Addresses the last review round:

- The three module level helpers arranging the client are gone. The cases now
  parametrize the tokens each validation request hands over, and a conftest
  fixture does the wiring, so the test body arranges in one line.

- The try/except around restoring a stored token is removed, along with its
  test. It could only fire if a future cookidoo-api changed the shape of
  CookidooAuthData, and a change like that is better met with a config entry
  migration than with a silent fallback to a credential login.

- Rebased onto current dev.

This is the last commit I will send to this pull request. I am withdrawing my
volunteer work on the project, so there will be no further rounds from me.

The branch is left in a working state for anyone who wants to carry it
forward: 81 tests pass, ruff, mypy and pylint are clean, and the upstream
library work this depends on is already released and needs nothing further
(cookidoo-api 0.18.1 through 0.18.4, miaucl/cookidoo-api#259, #262, #266
and #267).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GAQ727uX8BSNB1CPTEoGZE

ambiguous_rewritten_commits.message:
Bump cookidoo-api to 0.18.1 and persist the OAuth2 tokens

0.18.0 replaces the cookie session with a proper OAuth2 authorization
code + PKCE login that yields an access and a refresh token. Store them
on the config entry so a restart restores the session instead of
replaying the Cloudflare-protected credential login, and write them back
whenever the library rotates them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01U9tJdQdLB7bcvqpRp16LXC

Seed the OAuth2 tokens in a config entry migration

Address review feedback: move the initial token seeding out of the
coordinator and into async_migrate_entry, so the entry already carries
the tokens once the integration is set up. Runtime persistence of
rotated tokens stays in the coordinator.

Also broaden the exception handling in _async_setup. The cookidoo
exceptions are siblings rather than a hierarchy, so CookidooParseException
and friends escaped the CookidooRequestException/CookidooAuthException
handlers even though login() documents raising them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu

Revert the config entry migration, keep the setup exception handling

The migration request was withdrawn in review: the coordinator already
persists the tokens during _async_setup, so seeding them in
async_migrate_entry was redundant. This restores MINOR_VERSION 3 and
drops the migration and its tests.

The broadened exception handling in _async_setup stays: the cookidoo
exceptions are siblings rather than a hierarchy, so CookidooParseException
escaped the CookidooRequestException/CookidooAuthException handlers even
though login() documents raising it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu

Handle parse failures at the remaining login call sites

The cookidoo exceptions are siblings rather than a hierarchy, and a
recovery login() runs inside an except block, so the sibling
"except CookidooException" of the same try cannot catch what it raises.
CookidooParseException therefore escaped both the coordinator's
auth-recovery login and the calendar's, the latter reaching the service
caller as a raw library exception instead of a translated
HomeAssistantError. The calendar retry after a successful login was
unguarded for the same reason.

Also persist the tokens right after login() rather than after the user
info fetch, so a failure there no longer discards them and replays the
whole CIAM login on the next attempt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu

Persist rotated tokens on every recovery path

_async_update_data saved the tokens only after all four fetches
succeeded, so a rotation triggered by an early call was discarded when a
later one failed. Move the save into a finally, which also covers the
re-login branch. Since the tokens can rotate on any request, dropping
them can invalidate the stored refresh token and force a full credential
login after a restart.

The calendar's recovery login had the same gap, so save there too. This
means reaching the method from outside the coordinator; rename it to
save_auth_data, which also drops the _async_ prefix it never earned as a
sync function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu

Persist tokens rotated by a plain calendar fetch

get_recipes_in_calendar_week() can refresh and rotate the tokens on its
own, so saving only after the explicit re-login left a rotation from the
fetch itself unpersisted until the next coordinator poll. Move the save
into a finally, mirroring the coordinator, which covers the fetch, the
retry and the re-login alike.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu

Persist rotated tokens from setup and the entity actions

Any request can rotate the tokens, so the remaining call sites that
touch the client directly need the same treatment as the coordinator
update: the todo and button actions, whose failure paths never reach
async_refresh(), and _async_setup, where a restored token can be
refreshed just before the request that then fails.

The explicit save after login() in _async_login goes away, since the new
finally in _async_setup already covers that path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu

Replace the scattered token saves with a decorator

Every call site that touches the client had grown its own
"finally: save_auth_data()", which is the sort of thing the next one
forgets. Collapse them into a @persist_auth_data decorator, applied to
the coordinator setup and update, the calendar fetch and the todo and
button actions alike. Entities delegate save_auth_data() to their
coordinator so the same decorator fits both.

Also catch CookidooException in the two migrations, so a login that
fails to parse the CIAM page reports the same handled error as a request
or auth failure instead of escaping async_migrate_entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<email>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PrpVvVSMPvxivpbK1cZEeu
